title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not specified in the frozen preregistration), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariants violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, high prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation; such evidence motivates architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2]. This work asks a narrowly scoped, preregistered question suitable for a paired design: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with canary) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)?

We contribute: (1) a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a complete execution and analysis run (1000 complete pairs, deterministic reconciliation, and archived validator traces) with full accounting of model calls and repair stage counts; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation that reconciles the preregistered power assumptions with the observed high baseline validity and sparse repairs, clarifying what this specific estimand measures and does not measure. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run.
sections.related_work:
Empirical surveys and controlled experiments show that LLM outputs for structured tasks (code, configurations, plans) are susceptible to hallucination and prompt sensitivity that materially affect correctness [1],[2]. Work on constrained decoding and schema‑aware generation reports improved syntactic/executability outcomes in structured domains, though primary evidence often comes from non‑NetOps domains and transfer depends on validator/tool fidelity [3],[4]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers emphasize verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals aimed at mitigating automation risks; these works report prototype improvements while stressing dependence on validator coverage and protocol enforcement rather than on any single model alone [5],[6],[7].

Our study complements these works by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand measures the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a limited repair budget when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. This design avoids conflating downstream interventions with first‑pass prompt/decoding differences and thereby clarifies what downstream verifier/repair layers can and cannot achieve under tightly controlled conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design: The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration artifact is referenced in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements included: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered primary test was exact two‑sided McNemar applied to the 2×2 paired contingency table. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe. The preregistration's power_and_precision_plan explicitly targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 assuming baseline≈0.60 to achieve >80% power at two‑sided α = 0.05.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences: The archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate means both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Paired outcome differences therefore can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). This design does not measure any effect that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative constrained prompting arms that were not executed.

Model/runtime configuration and temperature caveat: The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator/digital twin was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0). The validator enforces workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus and validator semantics: Tasks were selected deterministically from the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile using the registered ordinal rule, producing 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 compares parsed candidate command sequences against manifest constraints in a deterministic digital‑twin emulator and produces structured validator traces archived per episode. Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary validity outcome required by the paired analysis.

Execution accounting, retries, and missingness: The preregistration and adapter contract limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}, cache_miss_count = 1005, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. The adapter's missingness_plan and the analysis executor's 'complete_pair_primary' treatment were applied exactly as preregistered.

Statistical analysis plan and prespecification fidelity: The preregistered confirmatory procedure is the exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 paired contingency table (conditioning on the discrete discordant counts). The paired bootstrap percentile interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. Important prespecification note required by reviewer request: the one‑sided exact McNemar was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration cand‑003‑stud‑001 and therefore any one‑sided McNemar result reported below is explicitly labeled exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory outcome; see the disclosure and preregistration artifact referenced above for exact preregistered texts.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting (artifact‑grounded): The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 1005; stage_counts record shared_initial_generation = 1000 and repair = 5. All deterministic consistency checks passed and cross‑condition cache reuse was not observed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test: The 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625: this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and sensitivity: The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The bootstrap interval excludes zero because bootstrap resampling on extremely sparse discordant counts can produce nonzero percentile bounds; the bootstrap summary was preregistered as descriptive only and is sensitive to small n10/n01 counts. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because this directionally one‑sided test was not prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 it is reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not change the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair mechanics and representative traces: Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑00000*.json) show the validator rejecting an initial candidate due to required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call, and the validator accepting the repaired candidate after revalidation. All corresponding raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the deterministic_reconciliation and execution manifests.

Contamination, exclusions, and missingness: The preregistered contamination checks and exclusion rules found no prompt‑leakage flags and no deterministic emulator errors; contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes. No post‑hoc exclusions were applied. All seeds and task_index selection rules were fixed pre‑execution per the preregistration.

Accounting implications for interpretability: Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). The small number of repairs constrains mechanistic inference about repair efficacy across failure modes; it also explains why paired discordant counts are sparse and why discrete conditional tests (McNemar) have limited sensitivity to very small absolute improvements when baseline validity is near unity.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive outcomes and preregistration fidelity: The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625), so H1 is not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive summary and excludes zero due to bootstrap sensitivity with extremely sparse discordant pairs; this descriptive statistic does not overturn the preregistered confirmatory result. Importantly, the one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) and is therefore labeled explicitly as exploratory/post‑hoc.

Power assumption mismatch and interpretive consequences: The preregistered power_and_precision_plan assumed baseline ≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15 to achieve >80% power at two‑sided α = 0.05. The observed baseline success rate (0.995) is far higher than that assumption; this mismatch substantially reduces the study's sensitivity to detect small absolute gains because near‑unity baseline rates produce very few discordant pairs. We therefore caution that the preregistered power calculation does not apply to the observed data regime and that the lack of two‑sided significance does not imply absence of any practical guarded benefit in scenarios with higher baseline failure prevalence. This reconciliation is drawn directly from the archived power_and_precision_plan and the deterministic_reconciliation artifacts.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics: Under the shared_initial_candidate design, only downstream validation and permitted repairs can create paired differences. The five successful repairs demonstrate that a deterministic validator with suitable coverage can correct particular ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair invocation count may reflect any combination of (a) few initial candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, (b) generator behavior for the chosen model+prompt producing valid candidates, or (c) validator coverage that does not capture other semantic error classes. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator rule sets.

Construct, internal, and external validity threats: Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; if the validator omits relevant policy checks, measured success rates may overestimate operational safety. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics correctly isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring prompt/decoding interventions. Execution fidelity: execution manifests record zero failed episodes and all deterministic checks passed, minimizing internal execution threats. External validity: the synthetic task corpus and a single model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments and other model families.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups: Artifact‑grounded evidence shows that verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend strongly on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups: (1) evaluate independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) include multiple model families to map model dependence. All follow‑ups should include power plans aligned to plausible baseline success rates and preregistered analysis choices.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar reported here (p = 0.03125) was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration and is presented as exploratory/post‑hoc. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
